title: The Southern Ocean
objective: After this level you can describe the ocean around Antarctica and its life.
summary: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current, Earth's largest wind-driven current, circles Antarctica and walls off the Southern Ocean. Its fish cope with antifreeze and, in icefish, blood with no hemoglobin.

cards.headline: Some fish in the Southern Ocean have no red blood cells at all.
cards.body: And they live in water cold enough to freeze the sea. To see how they manage, start with the current that fences their ocean in.

cards.headline: An ocean fenced by a current
cards.body: Remember Level 3: the Southern Ocean is the one defined by a current, with its northern edge at 60° south. That current is the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, the largest wind-driven current on Earth. It flows west to east all the way around Antarctica, the only current that circles the planet, linking the Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Oceans. It also works as a barrier, keeping the Southern Ocean apart from the waters to its north.

cards.fact: Antarctic icefish have no red blood cells and no hemoglobin.
cards.context: Hemoglobin is the protein that carries oxygen in your blood and makes it red. Icefish manage without it: they have bigger hearts and gill blood vessels, pumping extra blood to pull enough oxygen from the oxygen-rich Antarctic water. Most of the 16 icefish species live in the Antarctic.

cards.headline: Blood with antifreeze
cards.body: Level 72's seawater starts freezing at about −1.8 °C, and a fish swimming in it needs a way not to freeze too. In the late 1960s, biologist Arthur DeVries found the answer in Antarctic notothenioid fishes: antifreeze proteins that bind to ice crystals in their blood and keep the fish from freezing. The fish makes its own antifreeze, and carries it everywhere.

questions.prompt: Which way does the Antarctic Circumpolar Current flow?

options.label: East to west, along one coast only
options.rationale: It goes all the way around, eastward.

options.label: Around the North Pole
options.rationale: It circles Antarctica, at the other end of Earth.

options.label: West to east, all the way around Antarctica

questions.explanation: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current flows west to east all the way around Antarctica.

questions.prompt: Antarctic icefish have no hemoglobin to carry oxygen. How do they still get enough?

options.label: They breathe air at the surface
options.rationale: They are fish, taking oxygen from the water.

options.label: Big hearts pump extra blood through oxygen-rich water
Their antifreeze proteins carry the oxygen
options.rationale: Antifreeze stops freezing; it doesn't carry oxygen.

options.label: They sleep through the Antarctic winter
options.rationale: Nothing in their story involves sleeping it off.

questions.explanation: Icefish have larger hearts and gill blood vessels that circulate more blood, taking oxygen from oxygen-rich water.
